devon: Heads up — after the runtime rollout last night (kernel-selector v2 + new int8 quant-profile) we saw a ~18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for the chat-short workload between 03:00-04:00 UTC.

anika: I pulled the per-route metrics. Warmup hit-rate for 1-8 token prefixes went from ~84% -> ~66%. Latency bumped a bit too on p95.

ts-report-bot: ServingPerfBot snapshot: {
  route: chat-short,
  window: 03:00-04:00 UTC,
  prefix_cache_hits: 8123,
  prefix_cache_misses: 4300,
  hit_rate: "65.3%",
  baseline_hit_rate: "83.9%",
  kernel_variant: "auto-v2",
  quant_profile: "int8-fast",
  batching_mode: "adaptive-group-by-kernel"
}

alex: Noted. Could be keying differences after the kernel selector changed group-by semantics — we changed grouping from (model, version, seq_len) -> (model, kernel_variant, quant_profile, seq_len_bucket). If we accidentally include non-stable fields in the prefix key we can blow cache partitioning.

devon: I did a few local repros on canary: same request stream, old-runtime vs new-runtime. I dumped the raw prefix keys from KV store. Old keys look like: 
```
model=v1.2|prompt_hash=0x8f3a|seq=5|attn_impl=flash_attn|quant=fp16
```
New keys: 
```
model=v1.2|prompt_hash=0x8f3a|seq=5|attn_impl=flash_attn_kernel-3|quant=int8-fast-ao
```
So the kernel selector is appending kernel-specific suffixes that vary across machines/compiles. That explains miss fragmentation.

anika: Ugh. That means identical logical prefixes land in different key buckets depending on compiled kernel naming. Misses = fragmentation.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout "kernel-selector v2" -> canary (10%): success

alex: Two obvious mitigation paths: 1) Normalize key to only canonical fields (strip compile-time kernel suffixes and map quant profile aliases to canonical names) OR 2) Change grouping to route by logical kernel class (e.g., flash_attn) instead of compile id.

devon: Quick experiment: ran a patch that strips any kernel tag matching /kernel-\d+/ and maps int8-fast-ao -> int8-fast. Replayed 5k recorded requests against canary KV and hit-rate restored to ~82%.

anika: Can you paste the minimal patch you used? Want to prod on staging.

devon: Patch snippet: 
```
# pseudo
def canonicalize_prefix_key(meta):
  canon = {}
  canon['model'] = meta.model
  canon['prompt_hash'] = meta.prompt_hash
  canon['seq'] = meta.seq
  # normalize attn impl to logical backend
  canon['attn_impl'] = re.sub(r"(-kernel-\d+)$", "", meta.attn_impl)
  # normalize quant aliases
  qmap = {"int8-fast-ao": "int8-fast", "int8-fast-legacy": "int8-fast"}
  canon['quant'] = qmap.get(meta.quant, meta.quant)
  return "|".join(f"{k}={v}" for k,v in canon.items())
```

alex: Nice. Also ensure we exclude per-node compile hashes and timestamped flags (those were sneaky earlier).

anika: I ran the patch on staging; result: prefix hit-rate jumped from 68% -> 83% within the warmup window. No perf regressions in p50/p95.

ts-report-bot: PerfTestBot: staging-run: route=chat-short, requests=20k, prefix_hit_rate=82.6%, p95_latency_downstream=+0.8ms (noise).

devon: Root cause summary: kernel-selector v2 introduced compile-time variant tags into the kernel_variant string. Those tags were included verbatim in prefix key generation, causing fragmentation of KV partitions across kernels and quant alias churn.

alex: Follow-ups:
- Short-term: ship canonicalization patch to canary tomorrow morning and monitor.
- Mid-term: add a whitelist of stable key fields and unit tests that assert key stability across runtime binary permutations.
- Long-term: move to logical kernel classes for routing and expose a stable kernel_id in the runtime API (instead of compile hashes).

anika: I'll create the monitoring alert: if route prefix hit_rate drops >10% vs baseline in 5m window -> page oncall.

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-2483 "Prefix key normalization after kernel-selector v2" (assignee: devon)

devon: rolling the canonicalization to canary now. will report back after 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: Thanks. Also add a small eval harness to ensure quant-profile aliasing doesn't change keys — we missed that in the model onboarding checklist.

devon: canary is up; preliminary: prefix hit-rate on canary moved from 66% -> 81% in first 20m. No other anomalies.

anika: great. will keep an eye on p95.

devon: closing loop: will open PR with tests and reference vectors.

alex: Good postmortem once stable. Keep notes in the kernel-selector RFC too. :thumbsup:
